front: How large was the 2022–23 Attainment 8 score gap between Chinese pupils and White Gypsy or Roma pupils in England?

front: What examination is commonly used to select pupils for grammar-school places?

front: What does equality of opportunity in education seek to reduce?
note: The course explains that an equality-of-opportunity approach focuses on removing barriers.

front: What does an equality-of-outcome approach to education focus on?
note: The course describes the approach as focused on outcomes/results and their distribution.

front: At the same 70th percentile of age-11 attainment, how large was the grammar-school admission chance gap between the most affluent and deprived family fifths?
note: At equal 70th-percentile attainment, UCL reports 50% chance for the most affluent fifth and 15% for the most deprived; difference 35 percentage points.

note: Research design is affected by practical access-to-participants constraints; card applies this to a school gatekeeper.

front: How did the share of births registered to cohabiting parents in England and Wales change from 1986 to 2016?
document_page_or_section: ONS births by parents’ characteristics, lines 173–175
note: ONS reports a rise from 10% in 1986 to 32% in 2016.

front: How did the average age of first-time mothers in England and Wales change between 2006 and 2016?
document_page_or_section: ONS births by parents’ characteristics, lines 151–152
note: ONS reports 27.3 years in 2006 and 28.8 years in 2016.

front: How did the share of adults separated but still legally partnered in England and Wales change between 2011 and 2021?
document_page_or_section: ONS Census 2021 household and resident characteristics, legal partnership status, lines 192–196

front: What long-term trend did ONS report in the number of UK births since 1901?
note: ONS describes an overall tendency for the number of births to decline since 1901 while noting substantial variation.

front: In ONS’s analysis through 2018, how did death rates at all ages in 1901 compare with later rates?
note: ONS says mortality rates were historically much higher, with deaths at younger ages also more common.

front: What was life expectancy at birth for men in England and Wales in 1901?
note: ONS reports approximately 45 years for males in 1901.

front: In ONS’s historical series (1901 includes Ireland), what share of the population was aged over 64 in 1901 and in 2018?
note: The share aged over 64 rose from 5% in 1901 to 18% in 2018. The ONS note says figures before 1911 include Ireland.

front: In ONS’s historical series (1901 includes Ireland), how did the share of residents under 15 change between 1901 and 2018?
note: The share fell from 32% to 18%; ONS notes figures before 1911 include Ireland.

front: How did average completed family size compare for women born in 1950 and 1977 in England and Wales?
note: Average completed family size was 2.07 for the 1950 cohort and 1.94 for the 1977 cohort. The measure counts live-born children.

front: From 1994 through 2018, what migration trend contributed to UK population change?
note: ONS plots positive net migration from 1994 through 2018; figures beyond 2018 are not covered by that graph.

front: By what factor did the Jamaican-born population in England and Wales grow from 1951 to 1961?
note: ONS reports 6,000 in 1951 and 100,000 in 1961, more than 16-fold.

front: How did the unaffiliated share of the global population change from 2010 to 2020?

front: What do judges or magistrates decide after a defendant is found guilty?

front: What does HM Prison Service do in England and Wales?

front: In ONS’s historical series (1901 includes Ireland), how did the 1901 population compare with that in 2018?

front: What median-age gap separated people identifying as Christian and Muslim in England and Wales in Census 2021?
document_page_or_section: ONS Religion by age and sex, lines 90–93 and 109–112
